messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: I've been having Opus work on things of note (as have several others over recent days...)

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: I asked Opus if it could figure out why some fast moving pucks slide under the goalie in 94 when the goalie is in the butterfly animation.

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: This is the reason.

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: Posting here because it's probably the same in 95.

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: Basically, the save ability follows the animation. In this case, the stick gets moved far to the side by the animation.

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: A small area in front of the stick is checked. If the puck passes there, the stick deflects it.

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: If not, then the orange ring area is checked. If the puck passes through it, the puck is allowed to continue moving, even though in reality, the body part of the animation probably ought to block it.

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: It's not until the blue "body" part touches the puck that the save is made. There is a small sliver of blue at the front of the animation.

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: A fast moving puck, if lucky, can bypass this small sliver.

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: When the back of the body makes the save, it doesn't always hold the puck. Sometimes it merely blocks the puck.

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: The trick is that at this point, the puck is so deep into the goalie's body that the "blocked" puck gets pushed _backwards_.

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: And therefore winds up in the net.

messages.author: shawnmb
messages.text:
**The Hockey News**
*Season 18 Surprise Teams*

There have been some great surprises, and some not so great surprises in Season 18. Here are six that stand out.

messages.author: shawnmb
messages.text:
**1.    Big Four?**
Sumter, Pitt and Thunder Bay had a lock on top 3. But Taipei has jumped into the conversation as one of the league’s top teams. At 39-8-2-7 the Typhoons are guaranteed a top 3 seed, plus at 1.46 gaa they’ve locked down the lowest goals allowed in Season 18. Their first round matchup isn’t set yet, but you can book the under no matter who they play.

messages.author: shawnmb
messages.text:
**2.    Clinic is Open**
Betty Ford was yet to legitimately make the playoffs before Season 18. They were predicted to be a bubble team by a top-10 NHL 95 podcast. But then they went out and won 34 games, good for 74 points and a tie with Chalky (another pleasant surprise team!) currently at 6th. They might still fall a spot or two, but Krav is going to be a tough out in round one.

messages.author: shawnmb
messages.text:
**3.    Orange Blossom Special**
Orange County was predicted to not even be on the bubble. But the exi king showed that practice does pay off. They just missed, but at 24-23-3-6, Yoda has his first >.500 season ever. Really nice performance.

messages.author: shawnmb
messages.text:
**4.    Tankers unite**
On the other hand, South Hills, Italy and Richfield have forced everyone to think about tanking rules. This has been worse than watching last year’s NBA season. It was one thing when managers quietly soft-tanked. This is a whole different level. There used to be a thought that teams wouldn’t want to waste 3 months losing on purpose. Clearly, that isn’t enough disincentive.

messages.author: shawnmb
messages.text:
**5.    Missed out on playoffs**
Valhalla was a pre-season bubble team, and North Bay was a lock for playoffs. Both of them will miss. For North Bay, it will be the first miss in a long time. The shitty bill bracket is loaded.

messages.author: shawnmb
messages.text:
**6.    Returning Heroes**
LHX and Moses are showing that roster construction isn’t all its cracked up to be. Both of these guys have taken very bad teams and done amazingly with that. They are both locked in for the playoffs at 72 and 70 points respectively. Great seasons for both, and two teams no one will want to play in round one.

messages.author: shawnmb
messages.text:
**7.    Bonus Surprise**
Autobahn has been a decade of W out of the playoffs. But they’re back, baby! With a final day sweep of Minhattrick, the highway man clinches seed 16 and a first round matchup with Mr. Runner Up himself, Pink Elephants.

messages.author: Liasson to the Affairs of Gopher
messages.text:
📜 URGENT DIPLOMATIC UPDATE FROM THE OFFICE OF GAELIC GOPHER

I can now confirm receipt of 17 napkins from Sally’s Bar in Dinkytown, each purportedly containing the thoughts, wishes, and official positions of Mr. Gaelic Gopher regarding his Charter Status in the WN95HL League.

The napkins are currently undergoing careful review for authenticity, legibility, and possible beer-stain interference.

Given the volume of correspondence, I anticipate a thorough review will take some time. I ask the League to exercise patience as we work through this unprecedented diplomatic situation.

I will release Mr. Gopher’s official position when appropriate, assuming I can decipher the handwriting and determine which napkins are intended as binding declarations versus late-night amendments.

The Gopher has spoken. Apparently, at considerable length. 🏒📜🍻

messages.author: Liasson to the Affairs of Gopher
messages.text:
📜 URGENT UPDATE FROM THE OFFICE OF GAELIC GOPHER

A tragic development in the ongoing diplomatic proceedings: 9 of the 17 napkins received from Sally’s Bar in Dinkytown were too wet to be salvaged.

The cause of the damage remains under investigation, though preliminary theories include spilled beverages, rogue condensation, and what experts are calling a “highly concentrated Dinkytown incident.”

The surviving 8 napkins have been preserved and are being carefully reviewed by this office. Unfortunately, we cannot rule out the possibility that some of Mr. Gopher’s most important demands, grievances, and constitutional amendments have been lost forever.

I ask the WN95HL community to respect this difficult time and remember that behind every great league are great leaders, and behind every great leader are apparently 17 bar napkins.

We shall proceed with the surviving documents. The Gopher’s message will not be silenced. 🏒🍻📜

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: I explored something similar in 94 last week. An Up goalie makes a "shoulder" save but bobbles it and the puck goes in. Turns out it can happen because the goalie is like right on the goal line and the goal line logic causes the goalie to bobble the puck like _right_ on the goal line.

messages.author: Tickenest
messages.text: But it doesn't happen to the Down goalie because the bobbled puck gets pushed away from goal instead of towards it.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text: It’s the same in 95

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text: Bobbled pucks all get pushed up on the y axis.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text: So for an up screen goalie, that’s towards the net

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text: For a down screen goalie, it’s away from the net
